ko.executive_summary: Lambda deployed the first large-scale production CPO (co-packaged optics) cluster using Nvidia Blackwell GPUs at its Quebec facility with 10,000 GPUs, reducing network latency while maintaining throughput. Nvidia is leveraging photonics technology to rewire AI cluster interconnects, while industry faces a 1.6T optical module shortage driven by InP laser and DSP component constraints. Competing solutions including mmWave interconnects and strategic advisor appointments (Dr. John E. Bowers at Palomino Laboratories) signal growing competition in optical interconnect for AI data centers.
key_facts: Lambda deployed 10,000-GPU Blackwell cluster with CPO in Quebec
1.6T optical module shortage tied to InP lasers and DSPs
Nvidia has 15x capacity target for CPO plans (uncertainty noted by CEO exit)
Dr. John E. Bowers appointed to Palomino Laboratories Scientific Advisory Board
DECO unveiled mmWave ultra-high-speed interconnect for AI data centers
Meta developing distributed AI infrastructure connecting data center fabrics

implications.text: Lambda's first large-scale CPO deployment signals transition from prototype to production-ready AI cluster interconnect, validating Nvidia's photonics architecture for hyperscale.
InP laser and DSP bottlenecks limiting 1.6T optical module capacity expose critical chokepoints in CPO scaling; component sourcing will determine CPO adoption timeline.
mmWave solutions (DECO) and traditional optical paths both competing for AI data center interconnect market, fragmenting roadmap optionality for hyperscalers.
Nvidia CEO transition creates visibility gaps around 15x capacity CPO targets; reduced executive advocacy may slow ecosystem alignment around co-packaged standards.
Meta and Lambda investments in optical interconnect (CPO switches, distributed fabric) indicate hyperscaler confidence in photonics for AI cluster scaling despite supply constraints.

ko.counterpoint: Nvidia CEO exit raises questions about internal CPO roadmap commitment and 15x capacity ambitions, potentially slowing industry standardization and supply chain alignment.
